title: ¿Cuántas personas han vivido en la Tierra desde siempre? 🌍
staging_mode_proposal: stage: one figure on the Coral stage, multiplied with a pull-back at each step until the globe sits on the stage wrapped in rings of people.
curiosity_reason: The 'more alive now than ever died' line circulates as a fact and is false; enormous; puts the viewer inside the count.
hook_question: ¿Cuántas personas han vivido en la Tierra desde siempre?
false_belief: Hoy hay más gente viva que todos los muertos de la historia juntos.
turn: Scene 5: the living ring is one of more than thirteen; for every person alive, more than twelve have already lived and died.
closing_reframe: Los vivos no somos la mayoría: somos menos de uno de cada trece.
share_archetype: ese amigo que reenvía datos curiosos sin revisarlos
engine_reason: code3d on the asset route (engine selection: numbers spectacle by instancing): the sealed human-figure as the unit, instanced into rows and rings; the Earth as the library asset earth-globe (open job, sealed before production).
description:
¿Cuántas personas han vivido en la Tierra desde siempre? Más de cien mil millones, contando desde hace unos doscientos mil años.
Por cada persona viva hoy, más de doce ya vivieron y murieron. 🌍
Envíaselo a ese amigo que reenvía datos curiosos sin revisarlos.
wardrobe: human-figure standing pose only (sealed). The living: fig_shirt in the accent colour. The dead: one neutral grey for fig_skin, fig_shirt, fig_pants and fig_boots (a desaturated figure, no ghost or skeleton imagery).

scenes.name: hook
scenes.narration: ¿Cuántas personas han vivido en la Tierra desde siempre? Se dice que hoy hay más gente viva que todos los muertos de la historia juntos.
scenes.what_changes: One standing figure on the stage, lit in the accent; around it a crowd pops up row by row; the tag ¿MÁS VIVOS QUE MUERTOS? hangs above the crowd.
scenes.transformation: una persona sola → una multitud que aparece alrededor
scenes.camera: retroceso desde la figura hasta la multitud

elements.name: a person standing
elements.route: library human-figure, standing pose (sealed asset, sealed pose)

scenes.name: vivos
scenes.narration: Empecemos por los vivos: somos unos ocho mil millones. En fila, hombro con hombro, daríamos unas cien vueltas a la Tierra.
scenes.what_changes: The crowd forms a single file that runs off the stage; the camera pulls back until the globe sits on the stage and the file wraps it as a glowing accent ring, then a second, third... until a thick band of rings circles it.
scenes.transformation: multitud en el escenario → una fila que envuelve la Tierra muchas veces
scenes.camera: gran retroceso desde la fila hasta el planeta entero

elements.name: a line of people circling the Earth
elements.route: library earth-globe (open job) + human-figure instances along a ring, accent band at globe scale
elements.risk: medium-high: at globe scale the figures become a band; the near figures in the first frames are the cue; proof P1
aliases: line of people around the earth

scenes.name: antes
scenes.narration: Pero la gente lleva unos doscientos mil años naciendo y muriendo. Los demógrafos sumaron a todos los que nacieron alguna vez, generación tras generación.
scenes.what_changes: Behind the living ring, grey figures appear in waves, generation after generation, each wave standing behind the last, filling the stage outward like rings of a tree; a year counter runs backwards.
scenes.transformation: solo los vivos → oleadas grises de todos los que vivieron antes
scenes.camera: travelling hacia atrás a través de las oleadas, de los vivos a las más antiguas

elements.name: waves of grey people behind a coloured crowd
elements.route: human-figure instances, grey recolour, rows by instancing (pattern: 016 instanced heaps passed with a reference object in frame)
elements.risk: medium: a grey crowd may read as statues; proof P2

scenes.name: total
scenes.narration: La cuenta pasa de cien mil millones de personas. Si cada fila de vivos es una de estas vueltas, los que ya murieron envuelven la Tierra doce veces más.
scenes.what_changes: Back at globe scale: the accent band of the living stays; around it grey bands stack outward, one per eight billion, until more than twelve grey bands surround the single accent one.
scenes.transformation: una banda de vivos → más de doce bandas grises alrededor
scenes.camera: órbita amplia alrededor del planeta mientras se apilan las bandas

elements.name: the Earth wrapped in many bands
elements.route: earth-globe + stacked band instances (accent and grey)
elements.risk: medium: proof P1 (same staging, more bands)

scenes.name: giro
scenes.narration: O sea, por cada persona viva hoy, hay más de doce que ya vivieron y murieron. Más que un equipo de fútbol completo.
scenes.what_changes: The turn: back down to people scale: one accent figure stands on the stage; twelve grey figures step in around it one by one, lining up like a football team behind its captain.
scenes.transformation: una persona viva sola → rodeada por doce que vivieron antes
scenes.camera: bajada desde el planeta hasta una sola figura y órbita cerrada

elements.name: one coloured person surrounded by twelve grey people
elements.risk: low-medium: sealed asset and pose; a small group reads as people; proof P2 covers the grey recolour

scenes.name: cierre
scenes.narration: Así que los vivos no somos la mayoría: somos menos de uno de cada trece. Envíaselo a ese amigo que reenvía datos curiosos sin revisarlos.
scenes.what_changes: Single reframe image: the camera rises from the thirteen figures back out to the globe, where the one accent band is the thinnest layer of a thick grey shell.
scenes.transformation: trece personas → el planeta con una sola banda de color entre todas las grises
scenes.camera: retroceso vertical desde las figuras hasta el planeta

sources: People ever born: Population Reference Bureau, 'How Many People Have Ever Lived on Earth?' (Kaneda and Haub): more than 108 billion in the 2019/2020 update (table total 108,760,543,790); about 117 billion in the update dated to the November 2022 data (cited by secondary sources; FLAGGED: read the figure on the PRB page at the beat sheet). The narration says 'pasa de cien mil millones', true under both updates.
Start of the count: PRB begins its estimate about 190,000 BCE (FLAGGED: confirm the start date in the same PRB article); spoken as 'unos doscientos mil años'.
Living population about 8 billion: UN World Population Prospects (the 8-billion mark, November 2022).

Derived, not a source figure: dead per living person = (ever born - living) / living = (108 - 8) / 8 = 12.5 or (117 - 8) / 8 = 13.6, so 'más de doce' holds under both PRB updates; living share = 8/108 = 1/13.5 or 8/117 = 1/14.6, so 'menos de uno de cada trece' holds under both. The 'twelve more times around' line in scene 4 is the same ratio expressed as bands.

Derived: a file shoulder to shoulder at about 0.5 m per person: 8e9 x 0.5 m = 4 million km; Earth's equatorial circumference 40,075 km; 4,000,000 / 40,075 = about 100 turns. The 0.5 m shoulder width is an assumption, stated here; spoken as 'unas cien vueltas'.
simplifications: The rings of people are drawn as bands at globe scale; at that scale the figures are not individually visible.
The dead are shown as grey figures for the count only; every person who ever lived is drawn with the same figure.
flatness_test: 1. hook: one figure, then a crowd appears around it.
2. vivos: the crowd becomes a single file that wraps the globe in a band of about a hundred turns.
3. antes: waves of grey figures from earlier generations fill in behind the living.
4. total: grey bands stack around the globe, more than twelve for the single accent band.
5. giro: one living figure, twelve grey figures step in around it (turn).
6. cierre: pull-back to the globe: the accent band is the thinnest layer of a grey shell.
